I've only ever played the HD edition. Does the original have any qualities that make it better?
AOE2 vs. AOE2 HD which is better?

Depends on what you call original.

The original version, which is either Age of Kings (1999) or The Conquerors (2000) is basically the same game as HD, just in low-res and without Steam multiplayer. HD version changelogs can be found somewhere on Steam. Edit: found the changelogs: http://steamcommunity.com/app/221380/discussions

But there's also such a thing as the Userpatch (changelog), which is an unofficial update. Many of its fixes and features were intruduced in the HD version. IIRC, one of the Userpatch devs now actually works in the official HD team.

Voobly also has a different version based on the original one. I personally haven't tried it, but it's great, judging by replays on YouTube. It supports HD resolutions too, and has some amazing mods such as the spectator dashboard. Pro players generally play on Voobly.

Edit: to answer your question, I don't think there're any qualities that make the old original version better. Some people say that path finding is crappy in the HD, but that's a bug in the latest updates and it will probably be fixed soon. HD also has a different AI which is a bit smarter. But old AoC AI is available too, you can choose between them for each AI player.

TL;DR: All versions are great. Go to HD for official support and casual play. Go to Voobly for high-level pro play. Go to the original AoC for nostalgia.

Interesting to see this topic posted as it has been brought up amongst my FSU friends and on the message boards. Here is the consensus as to why Joe Mixon will play and Johnson will not.

Joe Mixon entered his plea just before a change in the Oklahoma law that changed what was allowed to be shown to the public via video recordings regarding an investigation and what was not.

Senator Holt had his bill regarding the release of dash cam videos to the public passed in early 2014. This law was able to exclude certain things videotaped in a licensed establishment with regard to the protection of the victim of a crime. A bill passed in early 2015 changed these criteria, but his plea was entered in between these two dates.

This law must have had an effect on the actual taping of the video for public consumption as it appears anyone who wants to see it can see it.

"The video was watched by journalists earlier this month following multiple open-records requests made before Thursday’s plea agreement. While it had not been released to the general public, anyone who made a request was allowed to watch the video through the Norman Police Department."

Maybe they can only show it to each person that requests to see it on an individual basis (which is why members of the media were able to see it?)?

I am by no means versed in the complex law of specifics of disclosure in police investigations in Oklahoma, but this is the gist of it. His video will not be seen by the general public, while Johnsons was. If he had a video out, I believe the team would have to let him go. I know there's an argument for "culture" and public perception with regard to each program, but this issue is too hot now to try to downplay if a gif could be spread of him punching out a girl.
